blocks.content: 11.1 UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Karnataka

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Covers UNESCO World Heritage Sites located within Karnataka.
Examines major regional dynasties and their distinct architectural styles.
Highlights key historical and cultural temples of Karnataka.

blocks.content: UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Karnataka

cells: Ruins of Vijayanagara Empire capital; Vittala Temple with stone chariot & musical pillars; Virupaksha Temple (still active); Hazara Rama Temple; Lotus Mahal; Elephant Stables; underground Shiva Temple; on banks of Tungabhadra
Chalukya dynasty (6th–8th century); 10 temples (4 Nagara, 6 Dravida style + 1 Jain); Virupaksha Temple (prototype for Kailasa Temple, Ellora); Papanatha Temple; Galaganatha Temple; Bagalkot district
Kudremukh National Park, Pushpagiri, Talakaveri, Brahmagiri, Someshwara, Sharavathi Valley Wildlife Sanctuary included; 6 serial clusters from Karnataka
Vesara style (hybrid of Nagara + Dravida); rock-cut caves; gradually evolved freestanding temples
Badami Cave Temples (4 caves: 3 Hindu, 1 Jain); Ladkhan Temple Aihole; Durga Temple Aihole; Mallikarjuna Temple Pattadakal
Kailasa Temple Ellora (greatest achievement); Cave 15 Ellora; locally Kashivishvanatha Temple Pattadakal
Further evolved Vesara; vertical layering; Trikuta (3 shrines) plan; elaborate sculpture
Trikuteshwara Temple Gadag; Dodda Basappa Temple Dambal; Amriteshwara Temple Annigeri
Star-shaped (stellate) ground plan; soapstone (chlorite schist); narrative sculpture bands; dense carving; no mortar used
Chennakeshava Temple Belur (1117 CE); Hoysaleshwara Temple Halebidu; Kesava Temple Somanathapura (trikuta); nominated for UNESCO WH
Distinctive tall gopurams (towers); pillared halls (kalyana mantapa); stone chariot; bas-reliefs of royal figures; brick & mortar + stone combination
Vittala Temple complex Hampi; Virupaksha Temple Hampi; Krishna Temple Hampi; Hazara Rama Temple
Persian + local fusion; bulbous domes; stucco decoration; arched gateways
Gol Gumbaz Bijapur (2nd largest dome globally); Ibrahim Rauza Bijapur; Bidar Fort; Asar Mahal Bijapur

Dedicated to Vishnu; 648 elaborate sculptures on outer walls; Darpane Sundari; took 103 years to build
Twin temples (Hoysaleshwara + Shanthaaleshwara); most extensive Hoysala temple; 30,000+ figures
Star-shaped trikuta; finest proportion; nominated for UNESCO WH inscription
3 shrines; Saraswati shrine has 'Gadag style' carving; well-preserved
Madhva Vaishnava pilgrimage; Ashtamatha; Paryaya (biennial head priest rotation); Kanakana Kindi window
Manjunatha Shiva shrine; secular management by Heggade family; all castes served; daily free meals to thousands
57-foot monolithic statue of Bahubali; largest free-standing monolithic statue in world; Mahamastakabhisheka every 12 years
Shakti shrine; pilgrimage on Mookambika Hill; Swami Vivekananda visited
Tall Gopuram (73m) with Shiva statue; Arabian Sea backdrop
Vaishnava pilgrimage; Cheluvanarayana Swamy Temple; Ramanujacharya spent years here
Major Shiva temple; annual Doddajatra fair; Nanjangud banana GI-tagged
Sarpa Dosha rituals; second most visited temple in Karnataka
